findings.evidence: Rollback for no-row-reorg paths clears `mysql.NotNullFlag` whenever `hasModifyFlag` is true: `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:397` + `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:399`, and `hasModifyFlag` is true when `ChangingFieldType` is set: `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:96`. But `ChangingFieldType` is set for lossy/checked skip-reorg changes even when NULLability is unchanged: `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:658` + `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:661` + `pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:662`. Clearing `NotNullFlag` weakens NULL enforcement in DML (`pkg/table/column.go:501`). Same pattern exists in other rollback helpers too (`pkg/ddl/modify_column.go:419`).
findings.fix: In rollback helpers (`rollbackModifyColumnJob`, `rollbackModifyColumnJobWithReorg`, `rollbackModifyColumnJobWithIndexReorg`), stop clearing `mysql.NotNullFlag` as part of “modify-column in-progress flag cleanup”. Only clear the in-progress markers (`PreventNullInsertFlag`, `ChangingFieldType`). If there are cases where `NotNullFlag` is set early in some path, guard the deletion narrowly (e.g., only when `PreventNullInsertFlag` was set by the job / when NULLability actually changed).
findings.impact: A failed `ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN` (skip-row-reorg / checked path) can unexpectedly flip an existing `NOT NULL` column to nullable after rollback, allowing NULL writes and violating prior constraints. This is a metadata integrity issue (schema changes despite DDL failure).
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked later history up to `upstream/master` (bab4993b6fd6): rollback code still clears `mysql.NotNullFlag` under `hasModifyFlag`, so this is not fixed later.
findings.verify: Repro idea (strict mode): `CREATE TABLE t(a INT NOT NULL); INSERT INTO t VALUES (1000); ALTER TABLE t MODIFY COLUMN a TINYINT NOT NULL;` (expect failure). Then verify `SHOW CREATE TABLE t` still shows `NOT NULL` and `INSERT INTO t VALUES (NULL)` still fails; with this bug, NULL insert may succeed post-rollback.
findings.what: Rollback cleanup for skip-row-reorg `MODIFY COLUMN` can clear an existing `NOT NULL` constraint when only `ChangingFieldType` was used as an in-progress marker (i.e., when NULLability wasn’t being changed).

subject: ddl: make some `MODIFY COLUMN` skip row reorg (#63465)
summary: Reviewed `a84aea0` vs parent with focus on DDL/metadata behavior around new skip-row-reorg / index-only-reorg paths for `MODIFY COLUMN`. Found one Blocker: rollback cleanup can drop an existing `NOT NULL` flag when the job used `ChangingFieldType` (but didn’t intend to change NULLability), causing schema integrity violation after a failed DDL.
